The American car maker, Ford, announced this week that they would be cutting 800 jobs in the UK and criticized the government's rules. These rules, called the zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) mandate, require car companies to sell an increasing number of electric vehicles each year. Ford said that this rule is simply impossible to carry out.

Female drivers, just like their male counterparts, have also been impacted by this situation. Interestingly, in 2022, Ford had supported the same policy it is now criticizing. The carmaking group had even suggested the British government to increase the sale of electric cars. They thought figures announced by the Department for Transport were not high enough. They believed that without higher targets, consumers, manufacturers, and investors wouldn't be encouraged to make or buy more of these cars. They worried that a decrease in these targets could negatively affect the expansion of charging stations.

However, Ford had also suggested that the policy should be reviewed if the situation in the industry changes. This fruit of reflection seems to have kicked in now as they seem to have changed their operation and views, due to the decreasing demand for electric cars. During the COVID-19 pandemic, with very low interest rates, car companies could sell as many cars as they could manufacture. The current reduction in demand was unforeseen. 

P.P.S: The changes in this industry have left Ford and others in a tough spot and represent a definite shift in business strategies from previous years. 

Any other questions?
